title: Race condition: concurrent runChecks invocations can interleave state updates
reasoning: While the refresh button is disabled when refreshing=true, if runChecks becomes async (as it should be for real API calls), a user could theoretically trigger a manual refresh just before the 60s interval fires, or the interval could fire while a manual check is in flight. Both invocations would race to setGroups/setLastRefresh, and the last write wins, potentially overwriting newer data with stale data if one check completes before the other.
reproduction:
1. Make simulateCheck async with artificial delay
2. Click refresh button, then immediately trigger interval (or vice versa via fast-forward timers)
3. Observe interleaved or out-of-order state updates
recommendation: Add a ref to track in-flight requests and bail early if already refreshing. Alternatively, use a single AbortController to cancel stale requests, or serialize checks with a queue.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist. This is a timing-dependent race condition that requires async checks and concurrent triggers.
suggestedRegressionTest: Test with mocked async simulateCheck and concurrent runChecks calls (manual + interval). Verify only one set of checks runs at a time and state is consistent.
